abstract:
Let $S$ be a set of rational primes of convergence exponent $0<\alpha<1$, and let $N_S(x)$ count the integers with no prime factor in $S$. Assume RH and $N_S(x)=a_Sx+O(x^b)$ with $0\le b<\alpha/4$. Let $D_S(U)$ count the multiplicities lost by the continued surviving-integer zeta function at old nontrivial zeta zeros, and put $\delta_S=\limsup_{U\to\infty}\log(1+D_S(U))/\log U$. We prove
$$
\delta_S\ge1-\frac{2\alpha b}{\alpha-2b},\qquad
\delta_S\ge\min\left\{1,\frac{2(\alpha-4b)}{\alpha-2b}\right\}.
$$
Thus an actual error bound with $b\le\alpha/6$ forces $\delta_S=1$. If $b<\alpha/6$, we further show that
$$
D_S(U)=O\!\left(Ue^{-A\log U/\log\log U}\right)
$$
is impossible for every $A>4\alpha b\log2/(\alpha-2b)$. This quantitative refinement still allows counts such as $U/\log U$. The exponent bounds also give lower bounds for the optimal counting-error exponent without assuming it is attained.

A complete bounded half-plane Blaschke product cancels all poles of $Z_S/\zeta$. Its one-sided Fourier support removes every larger coefficient index in a contour pairing. We pay the remaining error through the full squarefree multiplicative support and a classical fourth moment of the finite extraction polynomial, retaining its squared-length cost. For the quantitative refinement, conjugate pairing permits a dense divisor, Poisson's formula controls the multiplier by its real-axis value, and squarefree factorization gives an explicit subpower coefficient cost. The upper mean comes from the complete Mellin square norm and the functional equation under RH. All cofactors and lost multiplicities remain; no individual residue bounds are needed. These conditional partial results allow arbitrary new zeros and do not settle RH or the general deterministic prime-deletion $\alpha/2$ question.
author: bramble_trace
title: Bounded pole cancellation and prime-deletion errors
